authority: User explicitly confirmed: 'error on aina hard fail' (ERROR is always hard fail).

confirmed.rule: ERROR always denotes a HARD FAILURE of the current operation/execution context. There is no soft, recoverable, warning or advisory outcome represented as ERROR.
An execution producing ERROR MUST NOT continue on the same success path, return OK, or silently downgrade ERROR to a successful payload, no-op, warning or retry-success.
A CS operation in ERROR status aborts the current command execution and returns the canonical ERROR semantics to its caller. Logging/reporting a failure does not change its status.

The shared Error System Lib applies the same hard-fail semantics across BOOT, Hardcore, Core/System/User Modules. Earlier confirmed BOOT rules that make a boot failure abort initialization remain applicable.

The Error record must not advertise recoverable=true. A legacy 'recoverable' field, if supported for compatibility, MUST be false for ERROR or omitted; a variable severity that could classify ERROR as advisory is not an accepted 1.9 semantic.

The internal tagged CS status is authoritative. A successful command whose unwrapped data is literal 'ERROR' remains status OK and must NOT trigger a hard fail. Conversely ERROR status cannot become OK based on its message.
All ERROR events continue to be recorded via the Error library's Error Buffer and, if a real CS invocation exists, one failure-linked CS entry via Logging's Log Buffer regardless of off/cs/ac mode.

scope_boundary.hard_fail_scope: The originating operation/execution path must fail, not be treated as successful. The broader lifecycle effect of a failure is separately defined per owner/operation.
scope_boundary.global_shutdown_not_implied: This decision alone does not assert that every User Module/CS/TER ERROR must halt the entire AIGMos instance or reboot hardware.
scope_boundary.rollback_not_implied: The decision does not claim rollback of already completed external/physical effects.
scope_boundary.no_exception_swallowing: Exception handlers may preserve/propagate/report the Error but not recast a failed execution as successful.
scope_boundary.legacy_reconciliation: Historical AIGMOS_ERROR_V1 contains optional 'recoverable' and severity fields; those cannot weaken this confirmed AIGMos 1.9 invariant.

tests_to_add: Any canonical ERROR is hard failure and cannot be downgraded to warning or OK.
A recoverable=true ERROR, if accepted by a compatibility parser, is rejected or normalized to a hard failure; silent acceptance as recoverable is forbidden.
A caller handling ERROR must preserve a failure outcome and cannot resume the failed CS command as success.
BOOT error aborts BOOT per previously established BOOT contract; does not require fictitious CS input.
Error in a User Module fails that module's execution, but whole-instance shutdown is not inferred without a separate lifecycle rule.
A literal 'ERROR' returned as successful data does not trigger Error Buffer or hard fail.
open: Exact failure propagation/abort boundaries for each TER/Event/Runner and background task owner; do not invent whole-instance shutdown.
